title: Six Body Systems
description: Fourteen parts is too many to think about at once. Six systems is not, and each system lines up with the loop you already know.

content.value: Your body has a lot of parts too, and you never think about them one by one. You think in systems. The bones hold you up, the blood feeds you, the nerves carry signals.
Robots are grouped in exactly the same way. ARIA's fourteen parts fall into six systems, and each system has one job.

⚡ POWER      battery, switch            energy for everything else
🧠 BRAIN      controller board           reads sensors, makes decisions
⚙️ MOVEMENT   motors, wheels, driver     turns decisions into motion
👁️ SENSES     distance + line sensors    turns the world into numbers
📡 SIGNALS    LED, buzzer                tells you what it's thinking
🔩 FRAME      chassis, caster            holds everything in place
Tap a system below and every other part fades out. That is the fastest way to see which part belongs to which system.

content.title: 🎛️ Six systems, one robot

content.value: These are the same three boxes
Look at that list again. It is the sense, think, act loop from Module 1, this time made out of hardware.

SENSE  →  👁️ Senses          distance sensor, line sensors
THINK  →  🧠 Brain            controller board
ACT    →  ⚙️ Movement         motors, wheels
          📡 Signals          LED, buzzer

and two systems that make all of it possible:
          ⚡ Power            nothing runs without it
          🔩 Frame            nothing stays put without it
Signals sits under ACT for a reason worth pausing on. Lighting an LED changes the world, just as turning a wheel does. It is a small act, but it is still an act.
Power and Frame are the boring heroes
Neither of them senses, thinks or acts. They simply have to work. When they do not, nothing else gets a chance to.

A flat battery looks exactly like a broken brain from the outside. A loose chassis looks exactly like a broken motor. That is why an experienced builder always asks the same first question: is it actually getting power?
Remember this when things go wrong later. Check power and frame before you suspect anything clever. Most robots that "will not work" turn out to be a loose wire or a dead battery.
Key takeaway: six systems, each with one job. Senses, Brain and Movement are the loop itself. Power and Frame are what let the loop happen at all.

quiz.question: Which system does the controller board belong to, and which step of the loop is that?
options: Brain, which is the THINK step
Signals, which is the ACT step
Senses, which is the SENSE step
quiz.explain: The controller board reads sensor numbers and decides what to do with them. That is thinking, built out of hardware.

quiz.question: Why is the status LED grouped under Signals rather than Senses?
options: Because it sends information out to you, rather than bringing information in
quiz.explain: Direction is what separates them. Senses bring information in. Signals send information out. Lighting up is a small act.

quiz.question: Power and Frame do not sense, think or act. So why are they still systems?
options: To make the number of systems even
They are leftovers that did not fit anywhere else
Nothing else works without them. No energy means no motion, and no frame means nothing stays lined up
quiz.explain: They have to be working before the loop can run at all. That is exactly why they are the first thing to check when a robot misbehaves.

quiz.question: Your robot is completely dead. No LED, no movement, nothing at all. Which system do you check first?
quiz.explain: A flat battery or a switch left off looks identical to a broken brain from the outside. Always rule out power first, because it is the quickest and cheapest check.

quiz.question: Which system has the most parts on ARIA?
options: Movement, with two motors, two wheels and a driver
quiz.explain: Movement is five of her fourteen parts. Actually moving something takes more hardware than deciding to move.
